title: OpenCreds Item
description: One credential record: a login, a card, an identity, a note, a key, or an account. These are not six features but one record with a type and a named field group, so that everything the user typed lives inside a single encrypted blob. That is what makes password history free — it is an array in that blob, encrypted by construction, rather than a second table someone can forget to protect. Every field in every group is optional and defaults to an empty string, because a real vault holds half-filled records and a model that requires fields produces importers that invent them.

v.description: Item schema version, stamped into every record from the first write. A record you cannot identify is a record you cannot migrate. 1 for OpenCreds 0.1.

id.description: Generated on the client, because it is bound into the ciphertext as additional authenticated data. A ciphertext moved to another row fails to decrypt rather than silently showing the wrong credential.

type.description: Selects the field group. An item MUST NOT carry a group other than the one named here.

name.description: Display name. MAY be empty; importers fall back to the URL host when an export had none.

folderId.description: A folder declared in the same vault, or null. Folders are flat: a name may contain a slash and a client may render that as a hierarchy, but the model does not nest, because every product that nests disagrees about what a move does.

notes.description: Free text. For a note item this is the content.

fields.description: Custom fields. A hidden field is displayed masked; it is not encrypted differently, because everything in the item is already inside one ciphertext.

attachments.description: Attachment references, never bytes. An implementation that does not store blobs MUST still round-trip these.

history.description: Password history, newest first, defined only for login items. Capped at 20: the item blob is rewritten on every save, so an uncapped array grows the ciphertext without bound and the growth is invisible until sync starts timing out.

updatedAt.description: Belongs to the item, not to a transfer. An importer that restamps this destroys the only evidence of when a password was last rotated.

allOf.$comment: An item MUST NOT carry a field group other than the one named by its type. A card group on a login item is either a broken importer or an attempt to smuggle a field past a type-based permission check; neither should be stored. A false subschema is how JSON Schema says 'this property must be absent'.
Password history is defined only for logins.

itemType.description: Type codes 1 login, 2 card, 3 identity, 4 note, 5 key, 6 account. Codes 1-4 are fixed by a deployed vault and MUST NOT be renumbered; 5 and 6 are introduced by OpenCreds; 7+ are reserved.

key.description: Base64 AES-256 key the blob was encrypted under, held inside the item ciphertext so the blob store never sees it.

match.description: Carried so that a move does not silently widen where a credential will be offered. An implementation that does not autofill still round-trips it.

totp.description: An otpauth:// URI, or a bare base32 seed. Store the URI where you have it: it carries the algorithm, digits and period, and a bare seed loses them.

expYear.description: Four digits. Two-digit years from an import are expanded to 20xx.

ssn.description: National identity number. Named ssn for import compatibility; it is not US-specific.

keyGroup.description: SSH and PGP keys, API tokens, certificates, and the .env secrets that Credential Sharing synchronizes. path and mode exist so a restore is total: a private key written back with the wrong mode is a key ssh will refuse to use, and one written to the wrong path is a key nothing finds.

value.description: The secret for key types that are one opaque string (api, env, symmetric).

accountGroup.description: A provider account and the tokens that authorize acting as it. Deliberately not a login: a login is what a person types at a sign-in form, an account is what a machine presents to an API. They expire differently and are revoked differently, and conflating them is how a rotated refresh token ends up in a password history array.

provider.description: google, github, x, stripe, … An OpenOntology entity id where one is in use.

environment.description: production, sandbox, … A test key and a live key look identical and are not.
